title: Checks for the attempted use of the unary prefix increment (++) or decrement operator (--).
summary: Python does not support the unary prefix increment or decrement operator. Writing ++n is equivalent to +(+(n)) and writing --n is equivalent to -(-(n)). In both cases, it is equivalent to n. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.83.
message_templates: Python does not support the unary prefix increment operator (`++`)
Python does not support the unary prefix decrement operator (`--`)

title: Checks for assignments to os.environ.
summary: In Python, os.environ is a mapping that represents the environment of the current process. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.102.
message_templates: Assigning to `os.environ` doesn't clear the environment

title: Checks for uses of hasattr to test if an object is callable (e.g., hasattr(obj, "__call__")).
summary: Using hasattr is an unreliable mechanism for testing if an object is callable. If obj implements a custom __getattr__, or if its __call__ is itself not callable, you may get misleading results. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.106.
message_templates: Using `hasattr(x, "__call__")` to test if x is callable is unreliable. Use `callable(x)` for consistent results.

title: Checks for uses of multi-character strings in .strip(), .lstrip(), and .rstrip() calls.
summary: All characters in the call to .strip(), .lstrip(), or .rstrip() are removed from the leading and trailing ends of the string. If the string contains multiple characters, the reader may be misled into thinking that a prefix or suffix is being removed, rather than a set of characters. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.106.
message_templates: Using `.strip()` with multi-character strings is misleading

title: Checks for uses of mutable objects as function argument defaults.
summary: Function defaults are evaluated once, when the function is defined. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.92.
message_templates: Do not use mutable data structures for argument defaults

title: Checks for unused variables in loops (e.g., for and while statements).
summary: Defining a variable in a loop statement that is never used can confuse readers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.84.
message_templates: Loop control variable `{}` not used within loop body
Loop control variable `{}` may not be used within loop body

title: Checks for function calls in default function arguments.
summary: Any function call that's used in a default argument will only be performed once, at definition time. The returned value will then be reused by all calls to the function, which can lead to unexpected behaviour. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.102.
message_templates: Do not perform function call `{}` in argument defaults; instead, perform the call within the function, or read the default from a module-level singleton variable
Do not perform function call in argument defaults; instead, perform the call within the function, or read the default from a module-level singleton variable

title: Checks for uses of getattr that take a constant attribute value as an argument (e.g., getattr(obj, "foo")).
summary: getattr is used to access attributes dynamically. If the attribute is defined as a constant, it is no safer than a typical property access. When possible, prefer property access over getattr calls, as the former is more concise and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.110.
message_templates: Do not call `getattr` with a constant attribute value. It is not any safer than normal property access.

title: Checks for uses of setattr that take a constant attribute value as an argument (e.g., setattr(obj, "foo", 42)).
summary: setattr is used to set attributes dynamically. If the attribute is defined as a constant, it is no safer than a typical property access. When possible, prefer property access over setattr calls, as the former is more concise and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.111.
message_templates: Do not call `setattr` with a constant attribute value. It is not any safer than normal property access.

title: Checks for uses of assert False.
summary: Python removes assert statements when running in optimized mode (python -O), making assert False an unreliable means of raising an AssertionError. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.67.
message_templates: Do not `assert False` (`python -O` removes these calls), raise `AssertionError()`

title: Checks for break, continue, and return statements in finally blocks.
summary: The use of break, continue, and return statements in finally blocks can cause exceptions to be silenced. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.116.
message_templates: `{}` inside `finally` blocks cause exceptions to be silenced

title: Checks for single-element tuples in exception handlers (e.g., except (ValueError,):).
summary: A tuple with a single element can be more concisely and idiomatically expressed as a single value. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.89.
message_templates: A length-one tuple literal is redundant in exception handlers

title: Checks for exception handlers that catch duplicate exceptions.
summary: Including the same exception multiple times in the same handler is redundant, as the first exception will catch the exception, making the second exception unreachable. The same applies to exception hierarchies, as a handler for a parent exception (like Exception) will also catch child exceptions (like ValueError). Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.67.
message_templates: Exception handler with duplicate exception: `{}`
Exception handler with duplicate exceptions: {}

title: Checks for useless comparisons.
summary: Useless comparisons have no effect on the program, and are often included by mistake. If the comparison is intended to enforce an invariant, prepend the comparison with an assert. Otherwise, remove it entirely. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.102.
message_templates: Pointless comparison. Did you mean to assign a value? Otherwise, prepend `assert` or remove it.
Pointless comparison at end of function scope. Did you mean to return the expression result?

title: Checks for raise statements that raise a literal value.
summary: raise must be followed by an exception instance or an exception class, and exceptions must be instances of BaseException or a subclass thereof. Raising a literal will raise a TypeError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.102.
message_templates: Cannot raise a literal. Did you intend to return it or raise an Exception?

title: Checks for assertRaises and pytest.raises context managers that catch Exception or BaseException.
summary: These forms catch every Exception, which can lead to tests passing even if, e.g., the code under consideration raises a SyntaxError or IndentationError. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.83.
message_templates: Do not assert blind exception: `{}`

title: Checks for useless expressions.
summary: Useless expressions have no effect on the program, and are often included by mistake. Assign a useless expression to a variable, or remove it entirely. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.100.
message_templates: Found useless expression. Either assign it to a variable or remove it.
Found useless attribute access. Either assign it to a variable or remove it.

title: Checks for uses of the functools.lru_cache and functools.cache decorators on methods.
summary: Using the functools.lru_cache and functools.cache decorators on methods can lead to memory leaks, as the global cache will retain a reference to the instance, preventing it from being garbage collected. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.114.
message_templates: Use of `functools.lru_cache` or `functools.cache` on methods can lead to memory leaks

title: Checks for loop control variables that override the loop iterable.
summary: Loop control variables should not override the loop iterable, as this can lead to confusing behavior. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.121.
message_templates: Loop control variable `{}` overrides iterable it iterates

title: Checks for docstrings that are written via f-strings.
summary: Python will interpret the f-string as a joined string, rather than as a docstring. As such, the "docstring" will not be accessible via the __doc__ attribute, nor will it be picked up by any automated documentation tooling. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.116.
message_templates: f-string used as docstring. Python will interpret this as a joined string, rather than a docstring.

title: Checks for contextlib.suppress without arguments.
summary: contextlib.suppress is a context manager that suppresses exceptions. It takes, as arguments, the exceptions to suppress within the enclosed block. If no exceptions are specified, then the context manager won't suppress any exceptions, and is thus redundant. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.118.
message_templates: No arguments passed to `contextlib.suppress`. No exceptions will be suppressed and therefore this context manager is redundant

title: Checks for function definitions that use a loop variable.
summary: The loop variable is not bound in the function definition, so it will always have the value it had in the last iteration when the function is called. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.139.
message_templates: Function definition does not bind loop variable `{}`

title: Checks for abstract classes without abstract methods or properties.
summary: Annotated but unassigned class variables are regarded as abstract. Abstract base classes are used to define interfaces. If an abstract base class has no abstract methods or properties, you may have forgotten to add an abstract method or property to the class, or omitted an @abstractmethod decorator. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.118.
message_templates: `{}` is an abstract base class, but it has no abstract methods or properties

title: Checks for try-except blocks with duplicate exception handlers.
summary: Duplicate exception handlers are redundant, as the first handler will catch the exception, making the second handler unreachable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.67.
message_templates: try-except* block with duplicate exception `{}`
try-except block with duplicate exception `{}`

title: Checks for function calls that use star-argument unpacking after providing a keyword argument.
summary: In Python, you can use star-argument unpacking to pass a list or tuple of arguments to a function. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.109.
message_templates: Star-arg unpacking after a keyword argument is strongly discouraged

title: Checks for empty methods in abstract base classes without an abstract decorator.
summary: Empty methods in abstract base classes without an abstract decorator may be be indicative of a mistake. If the method is meant to be abstract, add an @abstractmethod decorator to the method. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.118.
message_templates: `{}` is an empty method in an abstract base class, but has no abstract decorator

title: Checks for warnings.warn calls without an explicit stacklevel keyword argument.
summary: The warnings.warn method uses a stacklevel of 1 by default, which will output a stack frame of the line on which the "warn" method is called. Setting it to a higher number will output a stack frame from higher up the stack. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.257.
message_templates: No explicit `stacklevel` keyword argument found

title: Checks for exception handlers that catch an empty tuple.
summary: An exception handler that catches an empty tuple will not catch anything, and is indicative of a mistake. Instead, add exceptions to the except clause. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.250.
message_templates: Using `except* ():` with an empty tuple does not catch anything; add exceptions to handle
Using `except ():` with an empty tuple does not catch anything; add exceptions to handle

title: Checks for exception handlers that catch non-exception classes.
summary: Catching classes that do not inherit from BaseException will raise a TypeError. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.255.
message_templates: `except*` handlers should only be exception classes or tuples of exception classes
`except` handlers should only be exception classes or tuples of exception classes

title: Checks for multiple usage of the generator returned from itertools.groupby().
summary: Using the generator more than once will do nothing on the second usage. If that data is needed later, it should be stored as a list. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.260.
message_templates: Using the generator returned from `itertools.groupby()` more than once will do nothing on the second usage

title: Checks for the unintentional use of type annotations.
summary: The use of a colon (:) in lieu of an assignment (=) can be syntactically valid, but is almost certainly a mistake when used in a subscript or attribute assignment. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.250.
message_templates: Possible unintentional type annotation (using `:`). Did you mean to assign (using `=`)?

title: Checks for set literals that contain duplicate items.
summary: In Python, sets are unordered collections of unique elements. Including a duplicate item in a set literal is redundant, as the duplicate item will be replaced with a single item at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: Sets should not contain duplicate item `{}`
Sets should not contain duplicate items, but `{}` and `{}` has the same value

title: Checks for calls to re.sub, re.subn, and re.split that pass count, maxsplit, or flags as positional arguments.
summary: Passing count, maxsplit, or flags as positional arguments to re.sub, re.subn, or re.split can lead to confusion, as most methods in the re module accept flags as the third positional argument, while re.sub, re.subn, and re.split have different signatures. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.0.278.
message_templates: `{}` should pass `{}` and `flags` as keyword arguments to avoid confusion due to unintuitive argument positions

title: Checks for dictionary comprehensions that use a static key, like a string literal or a variable defined outside the comprehension.
summary: Using a static key (like a string literal) in a dictionary comprehension is usually a mistake, as it will result in a dictionary with only one key, despite the comprehension iterating over multiple values. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in v0.2.0.
message_templates: Dictionary comprehension uses static key: `{}`
Dictionary comprehension uses static key

title: Checks for uses of mutable objects as ContextVar defaults.
summary: The ContextVar default is evaluated once, when the ContextVar is defined. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear and made it stable in 0.8.0.
message_templates: Do not use mutable data structures for `ContextVar` defaults

title: Checks for uses of delattr that take a constant attribute value as an argument (e.g., delattr(obj, "foo")).
summary: delattr is used to delete attributes dynamically. If the attribute is defined as a constant, it is no safer than a typical property deletion. When possible, prefer del statements over delattr calls, as the former is more concise and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bugbear. It is in preview.
message_templates: Do not call `delattr` with a constant attribute value. It is not any safer than normal property deletion.
